items.title: Case Report: Fulminant sintilimab-associated myocarditis complicated by complete atrioventricular block and suspected myositis-myasthenia gravis overlap syndrome.
items.authors: Pian Cheng, Xiaolin Zhao, Min Jin, Qinghua Lai, Jie Liu
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-associated myocarditis can cause life-threatening conduction disturbances and may coexist with neuromuscular immune-related adverse events. We report a 67-year-old man with stage IIIA lung squamous cell carcinoma who developed fatigue, bilateral ptosis, myalgia, weakness, and palpitations 13 days after his first dose of sintilimab following concurrent chemoradiotherapy. On admission, cardiac troponin T (cTnT) was 874.2 ng/L and creatine kinase-MB exceeded 300 μg/L. Serial electrocardiograms showed progression from bundle branch and fascicular block to complete atrioventricular block, profound bradycardia, and shock, despite a left ventricular ejection fraction of 54%. Coronary angiography revealed no obstructive coronary disease. The findings supported a clinical diagnosis of sintilimab-associated myocarditis with clinically suspected myositis-myasthenia gravis overlap syndrome; cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and confirmatory neuromuscular investigations were not performed. Treatment included intravenous methylprednisolone, immunoglobulin, mycophenolate mofetil, temporary cardiac pacing, and two limited-volume plasma exchange sessions (600 mL each). Infliximab (300 mg per infusion) was subsequently administered empirically for persistent myocardial biomarker elevation. Sinus rhythm returned, and cardiopulmonary and neuromuscular symptoms improved. Following withdrawal of immunosuppression, chest discomfort recurred alongside a cTnT rise to 299.4 ng/L, prompting resumption of corticosteroid-based therapy. At the latest follow-up on April 30, 2026, the patient remained asymptomatic with stable cardiac function, although cTnT remained mildly elevated. In ICI-associated myocarditis, a preserved ejection fraction does not exclude life-threatening conduction disease, and myocardial injury may recur after immunosuppression is withdrawn; continued ECG and troponin surveillance is therefore warranted.

items.title: Pembrolizumab-Associated Myocarditis and Myasthenic Crisis: Discordant Functional and Tissue Recovery.
items.authors: Allen M Yu, Billal Mohmand, Hend Bcharah, Conor Willson, Abeeha Naqvi, Zachary T Wilson
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) can cause myocarditis with overlapping neuromuscular toxicity. A 77-year-old man developed biopsy-supported ICI myocarditis with biventricular dysfunction (left ventricular ejection fraction: 36%) after 1 pembrolizumab cycle. The course was complicated by seropositive myasthenia gravis (MG) requiring mechanical ventilation and an unexpected nonocclusive saddle pulmonary embolism. Corticosteroid-refractory troponin elevation prompted escalation to abatacept, while prednisone was reduced for worsening myasthenic weakness. Follow-up cardiac magnetic resonance during sepsis showed improved left ventricular ejection fraction of 53%, but myocardial T2 remained elevated with a persistent nonischemic pattern of late gadolinium enhancement. Troponin remained elevated, and ventilator dependence persisted. ICI myocarditis may show improving ventricular systolic function while myocardial tissue abnormalities persist, and coexisting MG may limit corticosteroid use. Myocarditis and MG may coexist and require multidisciplinary management. Troponin T may remain elevated for months and is not diagnostic of ongoing myocardial inflammation.
items.zhSummary: 本文报告一例77岁男性患者在接受一周期pembrolizumab后出现免疫检查点抑制剂相关的心肌炎，伴有双侧心室功能障碍及血清阳性的重症肌无力，临床并发机械通气依赖及非阻塞性肺栓塞。心肌酶标持续升高且对皮质类固醇反应不佳，调整为阿巴西普治疗，同时因肌无力加重减少泼尼松剂量。随访心脏磁共振显示左心室射血分数改善，但心肌组织异常持续存在，且肌钙蛋白仍升高，机械通气依赖未解除。提示免疫检查点抑制剂相关心肌炎功能改善与组织恢复可能不一致，且合并重症肌无力限制类固醇使用，需要多学科协作管理。

items.title: [Nasopharyngeal carcinoma presenting with diplopia as the initial symptom mimicking ocular myasthenia gravis: a case report].
items.journal: [Zhonghua yan ke za zhi] Chinese journal of ophthalmology
items.authors: J Q Chen, Q Zhou, M Chen, Y Chen, J W Wang, J Chen
items.abstract: This article reports a case of nasopharyngeal carcinoma with diplopia as the presenting symptom, initially suspected to be ocular myasthenia gravis (OMG). The patient had fluctuating diplopia accompanied by bilateral limitation of abduction; diplopia resolved after the ice test. Further imaging identified a nasopharyngeal mass invading the skull base and cavernous sinus. Nasopharyngeal biopsy confirmed non-keratinizing undifferentiated carcinoma. The patient was treated with induction chemotherapy followed by concurrent chemoradiotherapy. During follow-up, diplopia disappeared, and bilateral limitation of abduction was ameliorated compared with baseline. 本文报道1例以复视就诊，初诊疑似眼肌型重症肌无力（OMG）的鼻咽癌患者。患者因波动性复视就诊，伴双眼外转受限，冰敷后复视消失。进一步影像学检查发现鼻咽部占位并侵犯颅底及海绵窦，鼻咽活检确诊非角化性未分化癌。患者经诱导化疗序贯同期放化疗，随访时复视消失，双眼外转受限较前减轻。.

items.title: Safety and Efficacy of Efgartigimod for Generalized Myasthenia Gravis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.authors: Ghazi Uddin Ahmed, Fnu Ramsha, Sejal Kinger, Jawad Ghias Shaikh, Fnu Prejna, Fnu Ritik
items.abstract: Severe muscle weakness is a hallmark of generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG), a chronic autoimmune disease that severely reduces quality of life. Traditional immunosuppressive treatments can have significant adverse effects and only partially relieve symptoms. Clinical trials have demonstrated the potential of efgartigimod, a neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) antagonist that lowers harmful IgG autoantibodies. This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed its efficacy and safety, analyzing randomized controlled evidence separately from uncontrolled real-world evidence. Up until August 2025, we conducted a thorough search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science, supplemented by the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) and ClinicalTrials.gov, for observational studies and randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating efgartigimod in gMG. Improvement in myasthenia gravis activities of daily living (MG-ADL), responder rates, adverse events, and quantitative myasthenia gravis (QMG) scores were the main outcomes. Placebo-controlled RCTs were pooled in two-arm meta-analyses (primary evidence) and uncontrolled cohort studies and case series in single-arm meta-analyses (supportive evidence), using random-effects models in Review Manager 5.4 and R (v4.4.2). Sensitivity, leave-one-out influence, and subgroup analyses were performed, 95% prediction intervals were calculated for single-arm outcomes, and the certainty of evidence was rated using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. The review was retrospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261518373). We included 11 studies (two RCTs, six cohort studies, and three case series) comprising 480 participants (385 efgartigimod-treated and 95 placebo-treated). In the RCTs, efgartigimod improved MG-ADL (mean differences [MD] = -2.62, 95% CI: -3.99 to -1.25, p = 0.0002) and QMG scores (MD = -4.59, 95% CI: -6.24 to -2.94, p < 0.00001) at peak effect, but the differences were not significant at the end of follow-up. MG-ADL responders were more frequent with efgartigimod than with placebo (risk ratios [RR] = 1.90, 95% CI: 1.40-2.56, p < 0.0001), including among acetylcholine receptor (AChR)-Ab+ patients (RR = 2.37, 95% CI: 1.61-3.47, p < 0.0001). The incidence of adverse events did not differ from placebo (RR = 0.93, 95% CI: 0.81-1.07, p = 0.29). Certainty of evidence was moderate for peak-effect, responder, and safety outcomes. In uncontrolled real-world studies, responses were observed in AChR-Ab+ and muscle-specific tyrosine kinase (MuSK)-Ab+ patients (MuSK-Ab+ pooled proportion = 0.781, 95% CI: 0.499-0.927; 18 patients) and corticosteroid doses decreased, but this evidence was of very low certainty. Single-arm estimates showed substantial to considerable heterogeneity (I 2 up to 98.8%) and wide 95% prediction intervals, although every contributing study showed improvement in MG-ADL and a reduction in corticosteroid dose. Randomized estimates were unchanged when restricted to the phase 3 ADAPT trial, which contributed 71%-92% of the statistical weight. In randomized trials, efgartigimod produces clinically meaningful short-term improvement in gMG with an adverse event incidence comparable to placebo. Because the benefit was not maintained at the end of follow-up, cyclical, individualized retreatment is likely required. Real-world data suggest benefit across serological subtypes and a corticosteroid-sparing effect; however, these uncontrolled estimates were heterogeneous and of very low certainty, and larger, longer term controlled studies, ideally conducted independently of the manufacturer, are needed to confirm these findings.

items.title: Antigen-presenting-cell-associated programs in thymoma-associated myasthenia gravis: public transcriptomic reanalysis and archived cell-model observations.
items.authors: Chao Lu, Yongjia Chai, Yuanguo Wang, Peng Zhang, Peng Zhang
items.abstract: Thymoma-associated myasthenia gravis (TAMG) involves a complex thymic immune environment, but tissue antigen-presenting-cell (APC) programs do not by themselves establish a soluble-signal mechanism. We re-analyzed public single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data and examined archived records from one Thy0517 AB-thymoma line and a THP-1-derived dendritic cell-like preparation. Donor-resolved single-cell summaries showed antigen-presentation-associated expression across several APC compartments, whereas IL21 transcripts were sparse and most evident in Tfh-like CD4+T cells. IL21R/IL2RG-containing modules were exploratory tissue annotations, not validation of IL-21R signaling in the culture model. In two TAMG sections, unadjusted APC antigen-presentation and maturation/costimulation correlations attenuated after covariate adjustment; associations with migratory DC, Tfh/IL-21 and GC-like B-cell programs differed between sections. A single normal adult thymus sample provided a descriptive, unmatched reference. The retained morphology and CD11c panels document induction of the THP-1-derived preparation, not an effect of subsequent Thy0517 conditioning. A separate cytokine worksheet contained IL-21- and IL-6-labeled entries, but concentration units and calibration could not be verified. Unverified quantitative marker endpoints were removed. Representative CD4+T-cell plots document the assay format only and do not establish frequency or ratio changes. These observations provide descriptive human tissue context and archived cell-model documentation; they do not establish a Thy0517-conditioning effect or an IL-21-specific TAMG mechanism.
items.zhSummary: 本研究针对胸腺瘤相关重症肌无力（TAMG）中的胸腺抗原呈递细胞（APC）程序进行了公开单细胞及空间转录组数据的二次分析，并结合了Thy0517 AB胸腺瘤细胞系与THP-1衍生树突状细胞样制备的存档记录。结果显示，多个APC亚群存在抗原呈递相关表达，IL21转录本稀少且主要来源于类滤泡辅助T细胞。IL21受体相关模块为探索性注释，未在细胞模型中验证IL-21R信号。APC抗原呈递及成熟共刺激相关性在校正协变量后减弱，不同组织切片中与迁移性树突状细胞、Tfh/IL-21及类似生发中心B细胞程序的关联存在差异。研究提供了人类组织背景及细胞模型文档，但未证实Thy0517条件作用或IL-21特异机制。这些结果主要为描述性，未涉及因果关系确认或疗效评价。

items.title: Pharmaceutical blockade of the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) ameliorates autoimmunity, inflammation, and fibrosis in the antitopoisomerase-I antibody-driven mouse model of systemic sclerosis.
items.authors: Cuong Tran Manh, Christoph Liebel, Aleix Rius Rigau, Bas van der Woning, Piotr Zabrocki, Jörg H W Distler
items.abstract: Several autoantibodies promote inflammation and fibrosis in systemic sclerosis (SSc). Efgartigimod, engineered to block the neonatal fragment crystallisable (Fc) receptor (FcRn) and reduce immunoglobulin G (IgG) autoantibody levels, is approved for autoantibody-driven generalised myasthenia gravis and chronic inflammatory demyelinating neuropathy. FcRn blockade with murinised efgartigimod (mEfgartigimod) and an FcRn-blocking IgG1 Fc fragment was evaluated in the topoisomerase-I (TopoI)-induced mouse model of autoimmunity-driven fibrosis. Effects were assessed by immunoglobulin levels, biochemical and histological fibrosis readouts, Olink analyses, RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq), and imaging mass cytometry (IMC). Both prophylactic and therapeutic mEfgartigimod ameliorated dermal and pulmonary fibrosis in TopoI mice, comparably to nintedanib. Bulk RNA-Seq analysis demonstrated FcRn blockade with mEfgartigimod downregulated inflammatory, autoimmune, and fibrotic signalling pathways, with reduced expression of Ccl chemokines, tumour necrosis factor superfamily cytokines, and type I interferon signalling components. IMC showed reduced accumulation of myofibroblasts, classically activated macrophages, dendritic cells, and T cells upon FcRn blockade. Single‑nucleus RNA-Seq revealed altered fibroblast-macrophage crosstalk, with decreases in myofibroblasts, inflammatory and neutrophil-like macrophages, and T cells with cell-type-specific transcriptional effects associated with reversal of profibrotic/inflammatory transcriptional programs. Consistent with these cellular changes, the circulating levels of Il1β and several chemokines were downregulated upon treatment, whereas antifibrotic mediators, such as Fgf21 and soluble Pd-l2, were upregulated. These findings highlight that FcRn blockers such as efgartigimod may have potential to simultaneously target autoimmune, inflammatory, and fibrotic features of SSc and highlight the potential of autoantibody-reducing therapies as disease-modifying approaches in SSc. A randomised, controlled phase 2 trial with efgartigimod in SSc is currently ongoing.
items.zhSummary: 本研究在抗拓扑异构酶I抗体驱动的系统性硬化症（SSc）小鼠模型中，评估了阻断新生儿Fc受体（FcRn）药物mEfgartigimod对自身免疫、炎症及纤维化的影响。通过免疫球蛋白测定、生化及组织学纤维化指标、多组学分析及成像质谱细胞术，发现预防性和治疗性FcRn阻断均减轻了皮肤和肺部纤维化，相关炎症和纤维化信号通路表达下调。细胞水平显示巨噬细胞、成纤维细胞和T细胞等免疫细胞及纤维化细胞数量及活性均减少。循环炎症因子下降，抗纤维化介质上调。研究提示FcRn抑制剂可能同时调节SSc中的自身免疫、炎症和纤维化，相关临床Ⅱ期试验正在进行中。

items.title: miR-155 expression associates with pathogenic circulating follicular helper T-cell phenotype in myasthenia gravis.
items.authors: Shinji Ashida, Hirofumi Ochi, Chihiro Fujii, Mio Hamatani, Toshiki Mizuno, Takayuki Kondo
items.abstract: Myasthenia gravis (MG) is an antibody-mediated autoimmune disease targeting neuromuscular junctions. We previously reported that ICOS-high expressing circulating follicular T cells (ICOShighcTfh) are expanded in MG and are associated with the disease severity. Although it is unknown what influences the skew of Tfh in MG, one of the candidates is microRNA (miRNA), especially miR-146a and miR-155, which were reported to be associated with accumulation and function of Tfh. Twenty-four MG patients positive for anti-acetylcholine receptor antibody and 12 HS were enrolled. The expressions of miR-146a and miR-155 in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) were analyzed by a real-time PCR system in association with the cTfh phenotype in MG. To further examine cell-type-specific MIR155HG expression, publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from MG patient PBMCs were analyzed. The expressions of miR-146a and miR-155 were significantly higher in MG than HS. The level of miR-155 but not miR-146a level showed significant correlation with the frequency of ICOShighcTfh. scRNA-seq analysis revealed that MIR155HG was most highly expressed in a Tfh-like CD4+ T cell cluster characterized by elevated CXCR5, ICOS, PDCD1, and IL21, which was expanded in MG relative to HS (24% vs. 18%), supporting the PBMC-level miRNA findings. miR-155 levels decreased after immunotherapy, paralleling the reduction of ICOShighcTfh in MG. Elevated miR-155 expression is associated with pathogenic activation of circulating Tfh cells in MG, supported by single-cell transcriptomic evidence of MIR155HG enrichment in a Tfh-like CD4+ T cell population.

items.title: Inpatient administration of complement inhibitors as rapid-acting therapy for recurrent or refractory myasthenic exacerbation: A case series, review of the literature, and discussion of pathophysiology.
items.authors: Julia Greenberg, Muhannad Seyam, Srikanth Muppidi
items.abstract: Complement inhibitors are primarily used for symptomatic/refractory but stable myasthenic patients in the outpatient setting, however there is emerging data to suggest that complement inhibitors may be an effective rescue therapy in acute myasthenic exacerbation or crisis. We present two cases of non-ventilator-dependent patients with refractory or recurrent myasthenic exacerbation in whom eculizumab was used as a rescue therapy, review the literature to date on inpatient use of complement inhibitor therapy for myasthenic crisis/exacerbation, and discuss the pathophysiology underlying rapid clinical response. Both patients had a rapid response to eculizumab with return of ability to speak and swallow within 48 h in one patient and reduction in MG-ADL score of >6 points within 2 weeks in one patient. Both achieved minimal symptom expression (defined as MG-ADL score of 0 or 1) within weeks and had sustained response to outpatient complement inhibitor therapy. Nineteen previously published papers (58 patients) were identified. Many patients had a clinically significant reduction in MG-ADL score or other objective evidence of clinical improvement within days, and had a sustained benefit with continued outpatient therapy. Our findings add to a growing body of literature suggesting that complement inhibition may be a useful, fast-acting therapy for myasthenic exacerbation in the inpatient setting in some cases. This rapid response is likely due to functional complement blockade in patients with complement mediated neuromuscular junction damage as a primary cause of MG exacerbation/crisis.

items.title: Rare paraneoplastic syndromes associated with thymoma: case reports and literature review.
items.authors: Xicheng Li, Dingxian He, Jie Song, Yiqin Xiao, Yu Xue, Yiqi Wang
items.abstract: Thymoma is the most common anterior mediastinal tumor, which is linked to the loss of self-tolerance and the presence of autoimmunity. Various interactions between thymoma and autoimmune diseases have been identified, including myasthenia gravis, systemic lupus erythematosus, pure red cell aplasia, and pemphigus. In this retrospective case series, we reported rare autoimmune disorders with different organ involvement associated with thymoma. These included ocular paraneoplastic pemphigus, neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, diffuse panbronchiolitis and myositis. Our series broadens the spectrum of autoimmune disorders with shared T cell-mediated and B cell-dependent pathogenesis, underscoring the recurrence or relapse of thymoma-associated autoimmunity. The recognition of rare autoimmune presentations charts future treatment decisions and multidisciplinary care.

items.title: Association of serum Sema4D and ANGPTL4 levels with disease severity and prognosis in myasthenia gravis patients.
items.authors: Wenqian Li, Mengsi Zhang, Zhibo Wang, Chundong Gong, Lu Sun, Wenjing Feng
items.abstract: To investigate the relationship of serum semaphorin 4D (Sema4D) and angiopoietin-like protein 4 (ANGPTL4) levels with disease severity and prognosis in anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody-positive myasthenia gravis (MG) patients. Between December 2023 and April 2025, 468 anti-AChR antibody-positive MG patients hospitalized at our center were prospectively enrolled and divided into good- and poor-prognosis groups according to whether they achieved minimal manifestations (MM) or better status at the 1-year follow-up. Healthy controls were also enrolled. Serum Sema4D and ANGPTL4 levels were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Correlations were evaluated by Spearman's rank correlation. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent risk factors for poor prognosis. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to evaluate the predictive value of the two biomarkers alone and in combination, and clinical and combined models were developed to evaluate the biomarkers' incremental predictive value. Serum Sema4D and ANGPTL4 levels were significantly higher in MG patients than in healthy controls (both p < 0.001). Compared with the good-prognosis group, the poor-prognosis group had higher proportions of Myasthenia Gravis Foundation of America (MGFA) class IV-V, dysphagia, and thymoma, and higher Myasthenia Gravis Quality of Life 15-item revised (MG-QoL15r) and Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) scores (all p < 0.05), and significantly higher levels of both biomarkers (both p < 0.05). Both Sema4D and ANGPTL4 correlated positively with MG-QoL15r and CONUT scores and with each other ( r = 0.431, p < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression showed that MGFA class IV-V, dysphagia, thymoma, higher MG-QoL15r and CONUT scores, and elevated serum Sema4D and ANGPTL4 levels were all independent risk factors for poor prognosis (all p < 0.05). The combination of the two biomarkers yielded an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.841, superior to either marker alone. Adding the biomarkers to the clinical model significantly improved prognostic discrimination, with the AUC increasing from 0.874 to 0.907 ( p = 0.0002). Combined measurement of serum Sema4D and ANGPTL4 is associated with disease severity and poor prognosis in anti-AChR antibody-positive MG and shows good predictive value for patient prognosis.

items.title: Targeted biologics in muscle strength restoration and corticosteroid sparing for patients post-myasthenic crisis.
items.authors: Ran Chen, Dingxian He, Huahua Zhong, Rui Zhao, Jianying Xi, Yan Chong
items.abstract: Myasthenic crisis (MC) represents a life-threatening condition in patients with myasthenia gravis (MG). Despite a substantial reduction in in-hospital mortality for MC, full restoration of muscle strength and quality of life usually requires months or years. It remains unknown whether the sequential use of targeted biologics improves clinical outcomes in patients post-MC compared with the standard of care (SOC). We prospectively followed patients from MC through 6 months post-discharge between November 2018 and November 2025. We then stratified patients into subgroups according to the use of either biologics-based therapy (C5 inhibitors, FcRn antagonists, or rituximab) (BIO) or SOC. The primary endpoint was the Myasthenia Gravis Foundation of America-quantitative MG (MGFA-QMG) score at 6 months after discharge. Secondary outcomes included Myasthenia Gravis Activities of Daily Living (MG-ADL), steroid dose, immunosuppressant (IS) use, cumulative steroid exposure, minimal symptom expression (MSE), and residual symptom burden. At 6 months after discharge, the BIO group (n = 56) had a lower MGFA-QMG score than the SOC group (n = 56) (4.51 ± 4.03 vs 6.28 ± 4.72; P = 0.038). Meanwhile, the BIO group required a lower dose of oral corticosteroid (14.74 ± 10.24 vs 21.96 ± 12.87 mg/day; P = 0.004), lower cumulative steroid burden (158.13 ± 64.71 vs 209.24 ± 96.81 mg/day·month; P = 0.001), and had a lower proportion of IS use (47.3% vs 67.9%; P = 0.028). MSE was achieved in 56.86% in the BIO and 60.38% in the SOC group, respectively. Targeted biologics were associated with better objective muscle strength and reduced corticosteroid and IS use after MC, although no significant between-group difference was observed in MG-ADL. A substantial proportion of patients in both groups continued to have residual symptoms at 6 months.

items.title: An mRNA-encoded bispecific T-cell engager targeting muscle-specific tyrosine kinase for myasthenia gravis.
items.authors: Yan Huang, Jia Zhang, Hongxiaoying Yu, Jianqi Zhang, Yongchao Zhao, Dong Xu
items.abstract: Muscle-specific tyrosine kinase antibody-positive myasthenia gravis (MuSK-MG) is a severe autoimmune disease with limited effective treatment options. We designed an mRNA-encoded bispecific T-cell engager (MuSK×CD3 TCE) comprising the human MuSK extracellular domain and an anti-CD3 single-chain variable fragment (scFv), delivered via a lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) to the liver to enable in vivo protein synthesis, which redirects cytotoxic T cells to eliminate B cells expressing anti-MuSK B cell receptors (BCR). In vitro, the MuSK×CD3 TCE mediated dose-dependent cytotoxicity against MuSK + target cells and induced robust T cell activation. In human PBMC-engrafted NOG mice, mRNA-LNP administration led to dose-dependent and specific inhibition of tumor growth in anti-MuSK BCR-positive tumors, with no significant impact on non-target B cells. Importantly, the TCE retained potent cytotoxic activity in the presence of physiological concentrations of MuSK autoantibodies-a key consideration for clinical translation, as patients with MuSK-MG typically harbor circulating autoantibodies. This "off-the-shelf" mRNA-LNP platform offers a precise, controllable and potent immunotherapy strategy for MuSK-MG and may be broadly applicable for other autoantibody-mediated diseases to eliminate pathogenic BCR + B cells.

items.title: Disease burden among patients with generalized myasthenia gravis in the United States receiving standard of care therapy: the patient perspective.
items.authors: Jacqueline Pesa, Louis Jackson, Alexander Keenan, Gregor Gibson, Hannah Connolly, Shiva Lauretta Birija
items.abstract: Examination of disease burden experienced by patients with gMG treated with standard of care and not with advanced biologics can inform treatment decision-making. A cross-sectional, online survey was completed by adults with generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG; patients self-reported a confirmed diagnosis) in the United States. Patients had received treatment with standard of care (acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, non-steroidal immunosuppressants, corticosteroids, rituximab, immunoglobulins, plasmapheresis) but not advanced biologics (eculizumab, ravulizumab, zilucoplan, efgartigimod, rozanolixizumab, nipocalimab). Responses were compared between patients with mild or moderate/severe gMG (Myasthenia Gravis Activites of Daily Living [MG-ADL] score 0-4 or 5-24). Linear elastic-net regression analysis explored associations between MG-ADL score and selected variables. Overall, 157 eligible patients completed the survey (87.3% female, mean [SD] age 49.5 [14.4] years, mean [SD] time since diagnosis 11.0 [10.9] years). Mean (SD) MG-QoL-15R score was 16.2 (7.2), EQ5D-5L score was 0.6 (0.3), and FACIT-fatigue subscale score was 20.2 (11.3). Overall, 51.6% received additional support/care. Patients with moderate/severe gMG (136/157 [86.6%]) had greater symptom occurence, reduced treatment satisfaction, greater health-related quality of life impairment, and greater support/care needs, compared with patients with mild gMG. In a regression analysis, gMG severity was associated with severity of health-related quality of life impairment (as measured by MG-ADL score and MG-QOL-15R score; coefficient 0.103 [95% CI 0.043, 0.191]). Patients in the United States with gMG who are receiving only standard of care report a significant disease burden and impaired quality of life, with greater impairment among patients with severe gMG. Myasthenia gravis is a rare autoimmune disease that causes muscle weakness. At first, the muscles around your eyes can become weak (called “ocular myasthenia gravis”) but over time muscles in other parts of the body can also become weak (called “generalized myasthenia gravis”). It is important to understand the symptoms faced by people with myasthenia gravis and how these affect their quality of life, because this can help physicians to decide which treatments would help them the most.In this study, 157 people with generalized myasthenia gravis in the United States were asked to complete an online survey, answering questions about different aspects of their disease and their lived experience. All had received “standard of care” treatments but had not received newer, advanced biologics called complement inhibitors and neonatal Fc receptor blockers. The survey responses showed that many people had eye symptoms, muscle weakness, poor quality of life, and a need for support from a relative. This was more likely for people with moderate or severe myasthenia gravis and less likely for people with mild myasthenia gravis.This means that some people with myasthenia gravis in the United States who are receiving “standard of care” do not have good control of their symptoms despite receiving treatment.

items.title: Urolithin A ameliorates experimental autoimmune myasthenia gravisin association with mitochondrial quality control-related and inflammasome signaling changes.
items.authors: Nan Zhang, Xiaotong Kong, Shihua Yu, Shanshan Peng, Guanghao Xin, Fanfan Xu
items.abstract: To characterize peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) remodeling in myasthenia gravis (MG) at the pathway and transcriptomic level, and to evaluate whether urolithin A (UA) ameliorates experimental autoimmune myasthenia gravis (EAMG) in association with altered mitochondrial quality control-related and NLRP3 inflammasome signaling. Single-cell RNA-sequencing data from two patients with stable MG and two with MC were analyzed. After quality control, 8414 stable-MG cells and 19,333 MC cells were retained. Cell composition, pathway scores, pseudobulk differential expression, gene-set enrichment, and ligand-receptor interactions were assessed. In parallel, EAMG rats were assigned to control, EAMG, EAMG+UA, or EAMG+UA + chloroquine groups (n = 6/group). Clinical, serological, inflammatory, ultrastructural, mitochondrial quality control-related, and inflammasome-related outcomes were evaluated. MC samples showed heterogeneous immune remodeling, including monocyte enrichment in one patient. Across immune-cell subsets, MC was associated with increased inflammatory, inflammasome/pyroptosis, oxidative-stress, chemotaxis, and lysosome-autophagy programs, whereas mitochondrial quality control-related changes were weaker and cell-type dependent. Exploratory analysis suggested enhanced TNFSF13B-TNFRSF13C interaction scores toward B-cell subsets. In EAMG rats, UA reduced clinical weakness, anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies, and pro-inflammatory cytokines; improved splenic mitochondrial ultrastructure and PINK1/Parkin-associated mitochondrial quality control marker profiles; and suppressed NLRP3/caspase-1/GSDMD-N signaling. Chloroquine partially reversed these effects. Exploratory scRNA-seq analysis of four patients suggests that MC is associated with pathway-level enrichment of inflammasome/pyroptosis and autophagy/lysosome programs, whereas mitochondrial quality control-related signals were weaker and cell-type-dependent. The EAMG findings support an association between UA treatment, improved mitochondrial quality control-related marker profiles, and reduced inflammasome activation.

items.title: Employment status and labour productivity losses associated with myasthenia gravis: an observational study.
items.journal: Archives of public health = Archives belges de sante publique
items.authors: Arnau Llauradó-Gayete, Francisco J Campos-Lucas, Irene Santamaría-Rodríguez, Juan Oliva-Moreno
items.abstract: To describe employment status and labour productivity losses among working-age patients with myasthenia gravis (MG) in Spain and to identify factors associated with the likelihood of being employed. We conducted a cross-sectional, multicentre observational study using a structured self-administered questionnaire distributed to patients with MG during routine neurology consultations between October 2023 and February 2024. Data on socio-demographic characteristics, clinical variables, self-perceived health status, and employment situation were collected. Multivariate regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with employment. Labour productivity losses were estimated using the human capital approach, based on age- and gender-adjusted employment rates from the general Spanish population. A total of 122 working-age patients were included. Although 96.5% had previous work experience, only 54.9% were employed at the time of the study, while 31.2% were receiving permanent work disability benefits. Higher educational attainment (+ 19.1% points) and better self-perceived health status (+ 34.9% points) were positively associated with employment. Treatment-refractory disease was negatively associated with employment (- 43.6% points). The estimated mean annual productivity loss per patient was €4,502.40. MG is associated with substantial reductions in employment and measurable productivity losses among working-age patients. The observed associations between clinical and patient-reported factors and employment outcomes may have implications for disease management, work capacity, and disability-related health policy, including strategies aimed at supporting labour market participation.

items.title: Delayed High-Output Chylothorax Following Thymectomy for Thymoma.
items.authors: Mourad Nafaa, Radia Bencherki, Jihane Ziati, Mustapha Noussair, Belyamani Lahcen
items.abstract: Chylothorax is an uncommon complication following thymectomy and results from disruption of the thoracic duct or its tributaries during surgery. We report the case of a 50-year-old man with autoimmune myasthenia gravis who developed a delayed postoperative chylothorax following video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) thymectomy for a type B2 thymoma, Masaoka stage I. On postoperative day 21, the patient presented with acute respiratory distress and severe hypoxemia. Chest computed tomography revealed a large left-sided pleural effusion with extensive passive lung collapse. Thoracentesis in the emergency department evacuated 1.5 L of milky pleural fluid, followed by an additional 4 L after chest tube drainage in the intensive care unit. Pleural fluid analysis revealed a triglyceride concentration of 188 mg/dL, with chylomicrons detected, confirming the diagnosis of chylothorax. The fluid also showed marked lymphocytic predominance (96%). Management included pleural drainage, a strict fat-free diet, and octreotide, administered as a 100 µg slow intravenous loading dose followed by continuous infusion at 50 µg/h. Pleural drainage showed an overall decreasing trend and eventually ceased. Octreotide was discontinued after 13 calendar days, and the chest tube was removed without requiring additional invasive or surgical intervention. The patient was subsequently discharged home. This case illustrates that post-thymectomy chylothorax may present several weeks after surgery and that conservative management may achieve a favorable outcome even in the setting of substantial initial pleural drainage.

items.title: AB027. Paraneoplastic diseases in patients with thymic epithelial tumours: findings from the nation-wide Danish thymic epithelial tumor database.
items.authors: Tine Østergaard, Eric Santoni-Rugiu, Thomas H L Jensen, Katharina A Perell, René H Petersen, Peter M Petersen
items.abstract: Patients with thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) are predisposed to autoimmune dis-eases, immunodeficiencies, and extrathymic malignancies. Still, the timing of these conditions relative to TET diagnosis and their prognostic significance remain poorly characterized. This nationwide study included all Danish patients diagnosed with TETs from 2015 to 2020. Data on demographics, tumor subtype, autoimmune diseases, immunodeficiencies, malig-nancies, follow-up, and survival were collected from electronic medical records. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize patient characteristics and disease chronology, while Kaplan-Meier analyses and log-rank tests were applied to assess associating with survival. Among 282 patients with a median age of 66 years, thymoma accounted for 85% of cases, thymic carcinoma for 14%, and thymic neuroendocrine tumors for 1.4%. Prior to TET diagnosis, 105 (37.2%) patients had a previous cancer diagnosis and 88 (31.2%) had autoim-mune disease. Over a median follow-up of 65 months, 33 (11.7%) patients developed new auto-immune diseases, and 41 (14.5%) patients developed new extrathymic cancers. The pattern of malignancies differed over time, with skin and colorectal cancers predominating before TET diagnosis, while lymphoma and prostate cancer were most frequent afterward. Myasthenia gravis was the leading autoimmune disease both before and after TET diagnosis, while Good's syndrome occurred only after diagnosis in six patients. Pre-existing autoimmune disease and pre-existing extrathymic cancer were not significantly associated with overall survival. A substantial burden of autoimmune and malignant disease was observed among patients with TETs, predominated by myasthenia gravis. Pre-existing paraneoplastic diseases were not associated with survival. A trend was observed in the incidence of certain disorders suggesting a shift in the pattern of developed paraneoplastic diseases after TET diagnosis.

items.title: Muscle Organoids Frontier: Construction Strategies and Applications of Multi-lineage Muscle Organoids and Multi-organoid Systems.
items.authors: Weijia Liu, Zitong Xie, Yuqing Sun, Mingxing Fan, Ling Wang, Quanzhong Ren
items.abstract: In recent years, multi-lineage muscle organoids have rapidly emerged as transformative research tools, providing high-fidelity models for deciphering skeletal muscle development and the pathological mechanisms of muscle diseases such as sarcopenia, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, and myasthenia gravis. Primarily derived from pluripotent stem cells, these organoids integrate multiple functional lineages, such as skeletal muscle, neural, vascular, and skeletal components, thereby addressing the limitations of conventional single-tissue muscle models. In parallel, multi-organoid systems, such as assembloids and organ-on-a-chip platforms, further integrate distinct organoids (e.g., muscle, skeletal tissue, tendon, and hindbrain/cervical spinal cord) to reconstruct inter-organ communication and systemic physiology under physiologically relevant conditions. By recapitulating in vivo-like multi-tissue interactions, they serve as critical platforms for drug screening and therapeutic development. This review summarizes recent advances in multi-lineage muscle organoids and multi-organoid systems, outlining their cellular sources, construction strategies, and major applications in basic research, disease modeling, and drug discovery, and discusses current challenges and future directions to enhance their potential in muscle research.

items.title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor induced Triple-M syndrome: A case series detailing what every ophthalmologist should know.
items.journal: American journal of ophthalmology case reports
items.authors: John Moir, Meghana Chalasani, Sunil K Srivastava, Amy S Babiuch
items.abstract: Immunotherapy has revolutionized cancer treatment but has also been associated with various immune-related adverse events. Triple M syndrome is a particularly rare and life-threatening adverse effect, which encompasses the overlap of immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced myasthenia gravis, myositis, and myocarditis. In this case series, we highlight the ocular manifestations of Triple M Syndrome, which, when recognized in conjunction with other systemic symptoms, can crucially lead to early diagnosis and intervention that may help to improve patient outcomes. Patient 1, a 69 year-old woman, presented with a 1-week history of bilateral ptosis and near complete ophthalmoplegia in both eyes 2 weeks after her second dose of combination therapy of Nivolumab and Ipilimumab for renal cell carcinoma. Patient 2, an 81 year old female, presented with a 3-day history of diplopia, right-sided ptosis, and bilateral partial ophthalmoplegia 2 weeks after completing her second dose of Nivolumab for cecal adenocarcinoma. Patient 3, a 69 year-old male, presented with a 2-week history of bilateral ptosis and poor peripheral vision 4 weeks following his first dose of Durvalumab for squamous cell lung carcinoma. All 3 patients progressed to Triple M Syndrome. Ophthalmologists may play an important role in identifying Triple M Syndrome, a rare but increasingly noted side effect of immune-checkpoint inhibitors. This case series highlights presenting symptoms that should prompt early recognition of Triple M Syndrome and also emphasizes the need for urgent referral to a multi-disciplinary care center for appropriate workup and inpatient management.

items.title: Good's syndrome and infections in a large retrospective cohort of thymoma.
items.authors: Wenji Jia, Lei Jin, Xiao Huan, Chong Yan, Jianying Xi, Liewen Pang, Chongbo Zhao, Jie Song, Xianglin Chu, Sushan Luo
items.abstract: Good's syndrome (GS) is an immunodeficiency associated with thymoma characterized by hypogammaglobulinemia. The co-existence of recurrent infections may be associated with quality of life and overall survival. Despite its relevance, the impact of GS on patients with thymoma has rarely been studied in large cohorts. This is a retrospective cohort study of patients with pathologically confirmed thymoma recruited between May 2010 and November 2024. Data on peripheral immune profile, infections, and paraneoplastic syndrome (PNS) were collected and analyzed. Of 1001 patients with thymoma, we ultimately included 158 patients who underwent peripheral immune profiling. The prevalence of GS was 45.6% (72/158), and the infections were reported in 43.69% (69/158). Infection rates were higher in the GS group than in non-GS group (50% versus 32.72%, P = 0.0384). Among the 121 pathogens identified from this cohort, bacteria were the most prevalent (52.07%, 63/121), followed by fungi (34.71%, 42/121) and virus (13.22%, 16/121). Patients with infections had significantly lower overall survival compared with those without infections (P < 0.001). In addition, patients with multiple PNS had poorer survival than those with a single PNS (P < 0.001). No significant difference in overall survival was found between the GS and the non-GS groups. GS and infections are prevalent in patients with thymoma. Infections and multiple PNS were associated with poorer survival outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of early detection and intervention for improving prognosis and long-term survival in patients with thymoma.
